cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me align that hinge. The door is dropping; tightening it at this angle will hold the mistake in place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Find it while I support the door. Give me the screwdriver, handle first, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. Hand me the tool and keep the door level; I would like something worth announcing.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 alignment correction and A3 tool handling establish A claimed repair competence as the reason B should surrender control; A5 redirects credit worry to proper repair.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 screw search causes A3 division of labour and tool request; B4 credit concern causes A5 announcement offer.

relationship.evidence: B2 still wants to complete the task and B4 fears loss of credit, giving A a meaningful resistance to address.

heightening.evidence: A5 grants B public announcement while assigning B door support and keeping the tool for A.

specificity.evidence: A1 sagging cupboard hinge and B2 screw task establish what A judges mishandled.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 something-worth-announcing is tied to B4 credit demand and the immediate support instruction.
